explanation: A heavy fast body (m=20, vx=60) strikes a light body (m=0.2) parked 0.1 from a thin 0.1-wide wall. The two-body collision impulses accelerate the light body to ~60 m/s in one step; the wall collision substepping/impulse then fails to stop it and its centre jumps from x=9.7 to x=10.82 across the [10,10.1] wall between steps 2 and 3, i.e. secondary impact velocity after a mass-ratio-100 crush exceeds the wall CCD handling.
